title: Mitigate transient starvation with leaky-reservoir admission and slot-aging weights
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Continuous-batching workloads occasionally trigger short-lived starvation where small, latency-sensitive requests get delayed behind larger KV-heavy merges. This creates visible p95/p99 spikes on interactive routes and forces us to overprovision for tail mitigation. Motivation: We need a light-weight admission and slot allocation adjustment that reduces transient hunger without impacting steady-state throughput or changing kernel implementations. This PR implements a leaky-reservoir admission gate combined with slot-aging weights and a conservative timeout-hedging policy to reduce starvation windows while preserving batching efficiency. Implementation summary: 1) Leaky reservoir admission: add a small, token-based reservoir that permits a bounded number of low-latency admissions per scheduling epoch. Tokens are refilled at a configurable rate and consumed when a request is admitted early. The reservoir decays rather than fully resetting on epoch boundaries so short bursts are smoothed. 2) Slot-aging weights: introduce an age multiplier for queued slots so longer-waiting requests gradually gain priority. We cap the multiplier to avoid starvation inversion and tune the curve to respect SLOs. 3) Timeout hedging: allow a jittered soft-timeout probe for requests near their deadline to trigger a lightweight hedged admission path. Hedging is only enabled when the leaky reservoir is low and system latency trends exceed a configured baseline. 4) KV-cache hotness hint: add an opt-in hint from the KV cache to the scheduler to mark known-hot pins as "sticky" so scheduling can avoid repeatedly evicting/prefetching KV entries for churny requests. This is a conservative hint only; core cache eviction strategy unchanged. 5) Metrics and observability: add new metrics admission.leaky_reservoir.tokens, admission.slot_age_multiplier, admission.hedge_probes, kv.hint_sticky_count and a dashboard tile for transient-hunger incidents. 6) Config: expose reservoir_capacity, reservoir_refill_rate, max_age_multiplier, hedge_timeout_ms and kv_hint_enabled in runtime config and Redwood Console.
Tests and validation:
- Unit tests: new tests covering token refill/consume behavior, age multiplier bounds, and hedging enable/disable.
- Integration: starvation_sim_test runs simulated mixed workload (short chat vs KV-heavy reranking) and asserts p95/p99 stability.
- Benchmarks: bench_batcher_latency.md includes before/after comparisons. Canary and perf results: staged canary in us-west2 and eu-west1 (2% -> 15% -> 50% -> 100%) over two weeks. Observed results on mixed KV-heavy production traces: p99 tail for small requests reduced by ~22% on canary nodes, p95 reduced by ~9%, overall token cost unchanged within 1-2%. Starvation incident count in synthetic repro dropped by 92%. No regression in throughput for large batch workloads; throughput changes within noise (+/- 3%). Rollout plan: staged rollout with circuit-breaker flags for reservoir and hedging. If any route shows >5% p99 regression we automatically revert feature flags for that route. Documentation: added docs/operations/batcher_tuning.md with recommended knob settings for common workload shapes. Backwards compatibility: all changes are opt-in via runtime config and safe defaults match current scheduler behavior. Performance impact: this is scheduler-only; no kernel-level compute changes. Implementation touches scheduler admission path, batching allocator, and lightweight KV hint plumbing. See files_changed for specifics. Merge notes: squash-merged after two approval cycles and a final canary pass.

review_comments: Evan Lin: Can you explain why a leaky reservoir is preferable to a simple priority queue bump? Concerned about oscillation under sustained load.

Aisha Patel: Reservoir smooths short bursts without permanently elevating priority; under sustained load tokens deplete and behavior falls back to age-multiplied queue. Added tests and doc note about oscillation and tuned refill_rate conservative by default.
Marina Kovalev: The hedged probe path looks risky for noisy latency signals. Add a smoothing window and require reservoir below threshold before hedging.
Aisha Patel: Added a 10s EWMA baseline check and an explicit reservoir threshold gate. Also added a feature flag to disable hedging per-route.
Derrick Wu: Need to ensure kv_hint is strictly advisory and doesn't create correctness dependencies on eviction order.
Aisha Patel: kv_hint is explicit and only affects scheduling preference; eviction logic unchanged. Added unit test asserting eviction invariants are maintained.
Evan Lin: Perf numbers look promising; can you attach the raw canary runs?
Aisha Patel: Uploaded raw canary traces to our S3 bucket and linked them in the PR description (internal).
summary: Introduces leaky-reservoir admission, slot-age weighting, and hedged probes to reduce transient starvation in continuous batching without kernel changes. Canary shows reduced tail latency for small requests with negligible throughput/cost impact.
release_notes: Added leaky-reservoir admission and slot-aging scheduler knobs to reduce transient starvation for mixed KV and small request workloads. Disabled by default for older deployments; recommended defaults enabled for new clusters.
canary_strategy: staged: 2% -> 15% -> 50% -> 100% across us-west2, eu-west1 with monitoring and auto-revert on route-level p99 regressions
observability_changes: New metrics: admission.leaky_reservoir.tokens, admission.slot_age_multiplier, admission.hedge_probes, kv.hint_sticky_count. Dashboard tile added to Redwood Console under 'Batcher -> Transient Hunger'
